import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import os
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import log_loss
import warnings

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# Set random seed for reproducibility
np.random.seed(42)

# Load datasets from input directory
print("Loading datasets...")
train_df = pd.read_csv("./input/train.csv")
test_df = pd.read_csv("./input/test.csv")
sample_submission = pd.read_csv("./input/sample_submission.csv")

print(f"Train shape: {train_df.shape}")
print(f"Test shape: {test_df.shape}")
print(f"Sample columns: {sample_submission.columns.tolist()}")

# Create hold-out validation split (stratified to preserve class distribution)
train_indices, val_indices = train_test_split(
    train_df.index, test_size=0.2, stratify=train_df["author"], random_state=42
)

# Split datasets
train_data = train_df.loc[train_indices]
val_data = train_df.loc[val_indices]
test_data = test_df

print(f"Training set size: {len(train_data)}")
print(f"Validation set size: {len(val_data)}")
print(f"Test set size: {len(test_data)}")

# Get author classes
author_classes = train_data["author"].unique()
class_to_idx = {cls: idx for idx, cls in enumerate(author_classes)}
idx_to_class = {idx: cls for cls, idx in class_to_idx.items()}
n_classes = len(author_classes)
print(f"Author classes: {author_classes}")

# Create TF-IDF vectorizers: word-level + character-level
print("Creating feature vectors...")

# Word-level TF-IDF (removed stop_words - common literary words have author-specific frequency patterns)
word_vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(
    max_features=20000,
    ngram_range=(1, 2),
    min_df=2,
    max_df=0.95,
    lowercase=True,
)

# Character-level TF-IDF (captures stylistic patterns like punctuation, letter patterns)
# MIN_DF=1 removed to keep rare character sequences that may encode unique authorial fingerprints
char_vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(
    analyzer="char", max_features=10000, ngram_range=(2, 4), min_df=1, max_df=0.95
)

# Fit word vectorizer on training text only
X_train_word = word_vectorizer.fit_transform(train_data["text"])
X_val_word = word_vectorizer.transform(val_data["text"])
X_test_word = word_vectorizer.transform(test_data["text"])

# Fit char vectorizer on training text only
X_train_char = char_vectorizer.fit_transform(train_data["text"])
X_val_char = char_vectorizer.transform(val_data["text"])
X_test_char = char_vectorizer.transform(test_data["text"])

# Concatenate features: [word_features, char_features]
X_train = np.hstack([X_train_word.toarray(), X_train_char.toarray()])
X_val = np.hstack([X_val_word.toarray(), X_val_char.toarray()])
X_test = np.hstack([X_test_word.toarray(), X_test_char.toarray()])

# Convert target to indices
y_train = np.array([class_to_idx[author] for author in train_data["author"]])
y_val = np.array([class_to_idx[author] for author in val_data["author"]])

print(f"Training features shape: {X_train.shape}")
print(f"Validation features shape: {X_val.shape}")
print(f"Test features shape: {X_test.shape}")

# Use the best C parameter found previously (C=10.0)
best_c = 10.0

# Train final model with best C on training data only
print("\nTraining final Logistic Regression classifier...")
model = LogisticRegression(
    max_iter=20000, multi_class="multinomial", solver="lbfgs", random_state=42, C=best_c
)
model.fit(X_train, y_train)

# Predict probabilities for validation set (for metric calculation only)
val_probabilities = model.predict_proba(X_val)

# Calculate multi-class log loss on validation set (hold-out split not used in training)
val_log_loss = log_loss(y_val, val_probabilities)
print(f"\nValidation multi-class log loss: {val_log_loss:.6f}")

# Generate predictions for test set
test_probabilities = model.predict_proba(X_test)

# Create submission file
submission = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "id": test_data["id"],
        "EAP": test_probabilities[:, class_to_idx["EAP"]],
        "HPL": test_probabilities[:, class_to_idx["HPL"]],
        "MWS": test_probabilities[:, class_to_idx["MWS"]],
    }
)

# Ensure submission directory exists
os.makedirs("./submission", exist_ok=True)

submission.to_csv("./submission/submission.csv", index=False)
print(f"\nSubmission saved to ./submission/submission.csv")
print(f"Submission shape: {submission.shape}")

print("\nSolution completed successfully!")
